headline: The traumas of 9/11: Veterans recount how the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq continue to have an impact today
lead: Hundreds of thousands of veterans returned from the wars following September 11, 2001. They are still struggling with their wounds today.
seo_title: 9/11 Veterans: The Continuing Consequences of the War on Terror
social_title: The forgotten veterans of the «War on Terror»: 25 years after 9/11
print_title: 25 years after 9/11: Wars that continue in people's minds
print_subtitle: After 9/11: War on Terror veterans continue to suffer from psychological wounds.
summary_bullets_en: Thousands of veterans continue to struggle with psychological and physical consequences of the post-9/11 wars, often including PTSD.
The U.S. government provides limited support, while facilities like the "Warriors Heart Ranch" offer rehabilitation assistance.
key_questions_de: Wie beeinflussen posttraumatische Belastungsstörungen die Veteranen?
Warum überlässt das staatliche System die Veteranen sich selbst?
Welche Rolle spielt die «Warriors Heart Ranch» für traumatisierte Soldaten?

original_de.headline: Die Traumata von 9/11: Veteranen erzählen, wie die Kriege in Afghanistan und Irak bis heute nachwirken
original_de.lead: Aus den Kriegen nach dem 11. September 2001 kamen Hunderttausende Veteranen zurück. Sie haben bis heute mit ihren Wunden zu kämpfen.

body.text: _Listen and subscribe to the podcast «NZZ Akzent» on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, or Castbox._

It began like any normal day for Sergeant Earl Lundy. The paratrooper was preparing food at the U.S. base in Afghanistan. Suddenly there was a white light, then darkness. Lundy found himself buried under meters of rubble. His leg was trapped under a steel beam. Doctors would later tell him he would never walk again. A suicide bomber had blown himself up, and two of his comrades died.

There are thousands of stories like Earl Lundy's. 25 years after the September 11 attacks, troops have withdrawn from Afghanistan and Iraq, but the wars continue to rage in the minds of the soldiers. Official sources indicate that over 40% of veterans suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, or addiction. However, the state system usually leaves them to fend for themselves after their wartime deployment.

U.S. correspondent Andreas Scheiner spoke with several veterans who went to war for the U.S. after 9/11. In the podcast «NZZ Akzent,» he reports on these encounters and his visit to the «Warriors Heart Ranch,» where traumatized veterans try to put their lives back together.
_All episodes of «NZZ Akzent» can be found in this overview._
